mutateBoundedIssueSuggestions.reason: Dedicated bounded writer for the scoped issue-record callback (mutateIssueScope contract) when it changes the scoped issues, appends their activities and edits, deletes or regenerates their issueSuggestions rows. Loads locked issue rows and their content rows, the display-refreshed image, complete policy fields, the scoped issues' suggestion rows with source ordinals, and referenced/declared users (ordered ID/Active directory with complete referenced values), labels, projects (triage fields) and states, or Complete sets for scoring callbacks. Validation refuses scope, team/number, other metadata, comment/notification and history rewrites. The suggestion patch removes regenerated issues' rows and appends the callback's rows, keeps other rows in place (in-place edits or deletions only), and persists through the legacy image writer, so fast-path point writes and the reorder full-field rewrite match the legacy delta writer; project progress, event (no previous values), realtime payload and resident publication follow the scoped point writer. Under WithIssueRenumbering the writer owns the team-move closure (scale_p21_issue_team_move.go, issueTeamMove): it locks the issue sequence first and passes max(installed NextIssueNumber, locked next) like the legacy writers, selects every possible target's (declared, the scoped issues' own, suggested and project teams) inherited workflow-state chain plus workspace states, labels named like the moved issues' or declared labels with their groups, and the documents attached to the scoped issues (with ordinals) plus their projects; issueTeamMove.check refuses moves outside those targets, renumbering without a move and document edits beyond IssueTeamID/InheritedTeamIDs with ErrIssueTeamMoveRefused before any write; RecordIssueActivity's merge into the latest issue.updated entry is admitted; the documents patch is persisted with the image and the sequence advanced after the issue rows. TestScaleP21TeamMoveAcceptDifferential (15), AutoApplyDifferential (7), ConcurrentSameTeam and KernelRefusals cover it. Differentials: state (18 cases), prune (6), regeneration incl. auto-applied assignee/project/label/relation and multi-issue order (5), each legacy vs warm vs SQL-reloaded with exact SQL rows, list order, events, webhooks and realtime; concurrent same-issue writers equal a sequential legacy order; persistent SQLite twice and -race.
